thread.title: Lenovo sinks 15% as China spy chip story resonates in Asia

author: morningstar.com
title: Lenovo sinks 15% as China spy chip story resonates in Asia
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
A report that the Chinese government embedded secret spy chips on U.S. computer servers continued to resonate on Friday, with Beijing-based Lenovo Group Ltd. coming under heavy selling pressure in Asia.
Shares of laptop maker Lenovo (0992.HK) finished the day down 15%, among the hardest hit as a swath of tech names across China and Hong Kong skidded (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-continue-to-sink-led-by-tumbling-tech-stocks-2018-10-04). Tech stocks were also hit in the U.S. on Thursday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-poised-to-retreat-from-records-after-five-day-rally-bond-yields-in-focus-2018-10-04), with concerns over rising U.S. bond yields also a factor for global equities.
Bloomberg reported Thursday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinese-operatives-were-able-to-infiltrate-motherboards-made-by-a-us-company-that-sold-to-apple-and-amazon-bloomberg-2018-10-04) that Chinese operatives were able to insert malicious microchips in motherboards made by Super Micro Computer Inc. (SMCI), which units of Apple Inc.(AAPL) and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) units bought products. All three companies denied the report, along with China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Plus:New cloud over Super Micro adds to its dark relationship with Wall Street (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/new-cloud-over-super-micro-adds-to-its-dark-relationship-with-wall-street-2018-10-04)
A spokesman for Lenovo told CNBC in a statement (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/10/05/lenovo-tumbles-after-report-about-alleged-chinese-spy-chips.html?__source=twitter%7Cmain) that Super Micro wasn't a supplier to the company "in any capacity. Furthermore, as a global company we take extensive steps to protect the continuing integrity of our supply chain." Based in Beijing, Lenovo bought IBM's personal computer business in 2005.
Read: U.S. judge orders China's ZTE to 2 more years of monitoring (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-judge-orders-chinas-zte-to-2-more-years-of-monitoring-2018-10-04)
Lenovo was ranked second last year in terms of market share held by personal computer vendors, just behind HP Inc. (HPQ), according to Statista (https://www.statista.com/statistics/267018/global-market-share-held-by-pc-vendors/).
The report that China may have infiltrated U.S. computers comes at a time of fraught tensions between the two countries. It broke hours ahead of a blistering speech by Vice President Mike Pence in which he accused China of meddling in U.S. politics. In a furious response on Friday, Hua Chunying, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman, said that Pence had "slandered" China (https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/10/04/us-says-china-wants-kick-trump-white-house/).
-Barbara Kollmeyer;
